doc_description: Adobe Systems Incorporated’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 2, 2016, detailing its shift to subscription cloud services (Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, Marketing Cloud) across Digital Media and Digital Marketing segments, 2016 revenue of $5.85B with 78% from subscriptions, key risks and MD&A, properties and legal matters, acquisitions (Fotolia; post-year TubeMogul), $1.9B in notes and active share repurchases, KPMG unqualified audit opinions, NASDAQ: ADBE listing, no dividends, and a Section 13(r) Iran sanctions disclosure (Bank Melli).

structure.summary:

Business: Overview of Adobe Systems Incorporated as a large, diversified software company serving creatives, marketers, knowledge workers, developers, enterprises, and consumers for creating, managing, delivering, measuring, optimizing, and engaging with digital content and experiences.
- Go-to-market and revenue models: direct enterprise sales and self-serve via app stores/adobe.com; SaaS/managed services (cloud/hosted), term subscriptions, pay-per-use; channel distribution through distributors, VARs, SIs, ISVs, retailers, developers, and OEMs; technology licensing to hardware, software, and service providers.

- Business overview and strategy: emphasis on transforming digital experiences and ROI; continued broad portfolio with investment focus on two strategic growth areas:
  - Digital Media: tools and services for individuals, SMBs, and enterprises to create, publish, and promote content; serves content creators, web designers, app developers, digital media professionals, marketing teams/agencies, companies, publishers, and knowledge workers; focus on integrated, cross-device workflows and evolving business models.
  - Digital Marketing: solutions for creating, managing, executing, measuring, and optimizing digital advertising and marketing across multiple channels; serves marketers, advertisers, agencies, and publishers.

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase: Founded in 1982, Adobe Systems Incorporated is one of the largest and most diversified software companies in the world.
structure.summary:
- Forward-looking statements caution, noting risks and uncertainties and SEC filings references.
- Company overview: Adobe’s history, global footprint, business model shift to SaaS/managed services, multiple channels (direct, web, app stores, partners), and broad customer base across geographies.
- Strategic focus areas:
  - Digital Media: tools and services for creating, publishing, and monetizing content; Creative Cloud as flagship; Document Cloud with Acrobat and Adobe Sign; integration of Adobe Sensei (AI/ML).
  - Digital Marketing: Adobe Marketing Cloud for analytics, personalization, content and campaign management, advertising and video; Sensei-enabled intelligence.
- Reportable segments: Digital Media, Digital Marketing, and Print & Publishing (mature/legacy offerings).
- Digital Media:
  - Market opportunity driven by mobile, bandwidth, social, and rich media.
  - Strategy to grow subscriptions, migrate legacy users, deliver cloud-first features, integrate Adobe Stock/Typekit/Behance, expand channels and enterprise ETLAs.
  - Document Cloud strategy to expand Acrobat/Reader services, e-signatures (Adobe Sign), and vertical/EMEA/APAC penetration.
- Digital Marketing:
  - Opportunity in delivering personalized, cross-channel experiences; shift of budgets to digital.
  - Adobe Marketing Cloud solutions: Analytics, Target, Social, Media Optimizer, Experience Manager, Campaign, Audience Manager, Primetime; Sensei for AI/ML.
  - Strategy centers on Personalization, Content, Advertising, and Data & Analytics; direct and partner-led go-to-market; TubeMogul acquisition to strengthen programmatic advertising.
- Print and Publishing: legacy eLearning/tech publishing/web dev/high-end printing; PostScript and PDF technologies licensed to OEMs; stable, mature revenue.
- Principal products and services detail:
  - Creative Cloud platform (Creative Profile, CreativeSync), Adobe Stock, mobile apps.
  - Key apps: Photoshop (incl. Elements, mobile), Illustrator, InDesign/InCopy, Premiere Pro (incl. Elements, mobile), After Effects, Dreamweaver, Animate, Muse.
  - Typekit, Behance/Portfolio, Adobe Spark (free entry).
  - Document Cloud: Acrobat DC, Acrobat/Reader (incl. mobile), Dropbox integration, Adobe Sign and integrations with enterprise systems and AEM Forms.
  - Marketing Cloud components: Analytics, Target, Social, Media Optimizer, Experience Manager, Campaign, Audience Manager, Primetime.
  - TubeMogul: single platform for planning, buying, measuring, optimizing ads (self-serve and managed).
- Competition:
  - Digital Media: numerous point tools, mobile apps, open source; competition from Apple, Autodesk, Corel, Microsoft, Quark, Getty/Shutterstock; OS/device bundling; social platforms and cloud storage encroaching; Document Cloud vs Microsoft, Google, Box, Dropbox; e-signature rivals DocuSign, Citrix.
  - Digital Marketing: large platform competitors (Google, IBM, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, SAS, Verizon/Yahoo!, Teradata), point solutions, in-house builds; agency/SI entrants; Adobe differentiates via breadth, integration, UI, scalability, and creative heritage.
  - Print & Publishing: competition from enterprise/XML publishing and low-end tools; OEM selection factors for print tech.
- Operations:
  - Sales via direct, adobe.com, distributors/VARs/SIs/ISVs/OEMs; global field presence; predominantly subscription revenue with some perpetual licenses; no 10% customer concentration.
  - Order fulfillment shifting to digital; remaining physical production outsourced (US, Germany, Singapore).
- Services and support:
  - Consulting/professional services, customer success management, enterprise maintenance/support, multi-channel tech support, premium services, partner enablement, and extensive training/learning programs (including subscriptions).
- Investments: selective stakes in private companies for strategic/financial returns.
- Product development: substantial, ongoing R&D investment; mix of internal development, acquisitions, and IP licensing.
- Product protection: IP portfolio (patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets); licensing models (per-user/device and SaaS); anti-piracy measures and activation.
- Employees: 15,706 as of Dec 2, 2016.
- Public filings access: investor site hosts SEC filings.
- Executive leadership: roster and bios of key officers (CEO Shantanu Narayen, CFO Mark Garrett, EVPs/CMO/CTO, segment GMs, etc.).
- Risk factors (excerpted): risks from failure to innovate/anticipate trends, platform shifts (mobile/tablet), competitive pressures and disruptive models, cookie/ad-blocking impacts, and uncertainties around subscription renewals.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase: As previously discussed, our actual results could differ materially from our forward-looking statements.
structure.summary:
- This excerpt is the Item 1A “Risk Factors” section of Adobe’s annual report, outlining material risks that could adversely affect operations, performance, and financial condition.
- Product and technology risks:
  - Challenges and costs of developing and enhancing products; need to anticipate changing customer needs and tech trends.
  - Dependence on third-party platforms and partners; adapting offerings to tablets/mobile and new OS/device releases.
  - Competitive pressures from new products, disruptive models (including low-cost/free alternatives), evolving standards, and industry consolidation.
  - Potential impact of ad-blocking and third-party cookie restrictions on marketing/advertising solutions.
- Subscription and revenue model risks:
  - Uncertainty in subscription renewals, churn, upsell/cross-sell success, and service reliability/security perceptions.
  - Timing of revenue recognition for subscriptions and ETLAs; multi-element arrangements and long sales/implementation cycles.
  - Risks in transitioning to new business models, pricing, open-source/standards strategies, and newer markets with less operating history.
- Macroeconomic and political risks:
  - Economic slowdowns, reduced tech/marketing spend, government budget cuts, credit market disruptions, and political instability.
- Sales execution risks:
  - Complex, extended enterprise sales cycles; quarter-end sales concentration.
  - Channel management challenges (distributors, OEMs), distributor financial health, and direct/government sales complexities.
- Security, privacy, and hosted services risks:
  - Cyber-attacks, vulnerabilities in products/systems, phishing/social engineering, data breaches, and associated costs, liability, and reputational harm.
  - Reliance on Adobe- and third-party–hosted services; potential outages, data loss/corruption, and failures to meet service levels.
  - Increasing global privacy/data protection regulation; cross-border data transfer uncertainties (e.g., Safe Harbor invalidation, Privacy Shield), potential fines, and dependence on customer compliance.
- Accounting and financial reporting risks:
  - Changes in accounting standards (e.g., revenue recognition, leasing) affecting results, systems, processes, and controls.
- M&A and marketplace risks:
  - Integration difficulties, retention of acquired talent/customers, due diligence gaps (IP, security, accounting), regulatory approvals, and culture fit.
  - Dependence of Adobe Stock and similar marketplaces on attracting/retaining contributors and customers; marketing effectiveness and technological shifts.
- Intellectual property risks:
  - Litigation and claims (including by patent assertion entities), unfavorable licensing, injunctions, and indemnification exposure.
  - Software piracy, source code disclosure, and challenges protecting trade secrets.
- Tax and currency risks:
  - Changes in tax laws/rates, effective tax rate volatility, audits (IRS/foreign), and transfer pricing scrutiny.
  - Exposure to foreign currency fluctuations; hedging may only partially mitigate impacts.
- Operational risks:
  - High-volume transaction processing accuracy and scalability.
  - Global compliance with varied laws (export controls, anti-corruption, data residency, PCI, antitrust, labor).
  - Multinational operations risks (foreign revenues/employees, IP protection, infrastructure, sanctions, localization, corruption, terrorism, pandemics) and scaling international footprint.
- Capital structure and valuation risks:
  - Debt obligations ($1.9B notes; $1B revolver), covenant compliance, and credit rating impacts.
  - Potential impairment of goodwill/intangibles.
  - Stock price volatility due to performance metrics, analyst expectations, competition, and market conditions.
- Catastrophic events and climate change:
  - Disaster risks (earthquakes in Bay Area/Salt Lake, cyber events) impacting data centers and operations.
  - Climate change impacts (droughts in California/India), resource access, regulatory/environmental considerations.
- Investment portfolio risk:
  - Potential impairment from deteriorating financial markets despite conservative investment policies.
- Item 1B “Unresolved Staff Comments”: None.

structure.summary:
- Risk factors: potential impairment of goodwill and amortizable intangibles could negatively impact results; heavy reliance on internal IT, network infrastructure, website, and third‑party hosted services exposes the company to disruptions from cyberattacks, system failures, power/telecom outages, and catastrophic events (e.g., earthquakes, fires, floods, tsunamis, war, terrorism). Geographic concentration near major earthquake faults in the San Francisco Bay Area and Salt Lake Valley heightens exposure. Possible impacts include service interruptions, reputational harm, IP loss, data breaches, development delays, and reduced demand.
- Climate change: vulnerability to prolonged droughts in California and India may limit access to clean water and reliable energy, causing operational disruptions, recovery time, and added costs. Regulatory and environmental shifts could influence office locations, partner choices, and product/service delivery.
- Investment portfolio: as of December 2, 2016, holdings included corporate bonds/commercial paper, U.S. agency and Treasury securities, money market funds, municipals, time deposits, and asset‑backed securities. An established investment policy mitigates interest rate and credit risk, but deteriorating markets could impair investments and increase other income/expense volatility. No material impairments as of that date, but future conditions are uncertain.
- SEC matters: no unresolved staff comments (Item 1B).
- Properties (Item 2): mix of owned and leased facilities worldwide; most leases are operating leases expiring through 2031 (with a Noida, India land lease to 2091); annual base rent approximately $88.5 million, subject to adjustments and interest rates. Key sites and uses:
  - San Jose, CA headquarters (East and West Towers owned; Almaden Tower leased) for research, product development, sales, marketing, administration.
  - San Francisco, CA (601/625 Townsend; 410 Townsend) for similar functions.
  - Seattle, WA for product development, sales, marketing, technical support, administration.
  - Lehi, UT; New York, NY; Ottawa, Canada for R&D and go‑to‑market functions.
  - Hillsboro, OR data center.
  - India: multiple Noida campuses and Bangalore facility for product development, research, sales, administration.
  - Tokyo, Japan and Maidenhead, UK offices for product development, sales, marketing, administration.

structure.title: Properties
structure.heading: Item 2. Properties
structure.start_phrase: We occupy three office buildings in San Jose, California where our corporate headquarters sit.
structure.summary:
- Item 2. Properties: Describes Adobe’s global real estate portfolio and usage. Corporate headquarters span three towers in San Jose, CA (own East/West Towers; lease Almaden; own underlying land). Additional owned sites include Lehi, UT; 601/625 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA; and a data center in Hillsboro, OR. Outside the U.S., Adobe owns facilities/land in Bangalore and Noida, India, with other offices leased worldwide (Japan, UK, Canada, Seattle, New York, San Francisco). All leases are operating leases, generally expiring through 2031 (Noida land lease to 2091). Annual base rent for leased facilities is about $88.5 million, subject to adjustments and interest rate changes. Facilities are in good condition and operating at approximately 86% capacity. Notable footnotes: in Ottawa, Adobe occupies ~48% of a 122,000 sq. ft. facility (with some space subleased and 6,000 sq. ft. unoccupied); in August 2016, Noida operations were consolidated into the Adobe Towers (Sector 25A). The listed properties support research, product development, sales, marketing, technical support, administration, and include a dedicated data center.

- Item 3. Legal Proceedings: Outlines exposure to intellectual property disputes (including patents) and other routine commercial/employment matters. Emphasizes potential impacts (liabilities, unfavorable licensing, injunctions, operational disruption, indemnification obligations) and the company’s GAAP-based process for assessing, disclosing, and accruing losses (provisions recorded when probable and estimable; reviewed at least quarterly with the Audit Committee and external auditors). Legal costs are expensed as incurred. While Adobe believes it has valid defenses, adverse outcomes could negatively affect financial position, cash flows, or results. Anti-piracy actions may trigger counterclaims, which also pose potential financial impacts.

- Item 4. Mine Safety Disclosures: Not applicable.

structure.heading: Item 3. Legal Proceedings

structure.summary:

- Legal proceedings (Item 3): The company faces current and potential disputes, particularly around third-party intellectual property (including patents), which can be costly and disruptive. Potential outcomes include liabilities, unfavorable licensing terms, injunctions, operational disruptions, and indemnification obligations to customers.
- Claims assessment and accounting: Claims are reviewed quarterly under GAAP to determine whether losses are reasonably possible, probable, and estimable. Provisions are recorded when losses are both probable and reasonably estimable, and are updated based on negotiations, settlements, rulings, and counsel advice. Decisions are reviewed with the Audit Committee and the independent auditor. No accrual/disclosure is made when losses beyond amounts recognized are not reasonably possible, cannot be estimated, or are immaterial. Legal costs are expensed as incurred.
- Litigation outlook: While the company believes it has valid defenses, unfavorable outcomes could negatively affect financial position, cash flows, or results of operations.
- Anti-piracy enforcement: The company pursues actions against alleged copyright infringement (including via the Business Software Alliance), which may prompt counterclaims; these could negatively impact results in a given period despite asserted defenses.
- Mine Safety Disclosures (Item 4): Not applicable.

  - Acquisitions:

structure.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes thereto.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Item 7 MD&A covering financial condition and results of operations, with references to consolidated financial statements and notes.

- Acquisitions:
  - Fotolia (royalty-free stock marketplace) acquired in 2015 for $807.5M, integrated into Digital Media.
  - Other immaterial acquisitions in 2014–2016.
  - Post year-end: TubeMogul (video advertising platform) acquired for ~$549M cash; to be integrated into Digital Marketing in Q1 FY2017; initial purchase accounting pending.

- Critical accounting policies and estimates:
  - Revenue recognition for subscriptions, hosted services, software licenses, maintenance, consulting, and training; multiple-element arrangements using VSOE/TPE/BESP; estimates for returns, rebates, price protection, royalties.
  - Business combinations: purchase price allocation to tangible/intangible assets, deferred revenue, and assumed equity; valuation methods and key assumptions (cash flows, development costs, discount rates, trademarks); equity awards valued with a modified binomial model.
  - Goodwill impairment: annual test; no impairment in FY2016 with fair values well above carrying values.
  - Income taxes: asset/liability method; reserves for uncertain tax positions; permanent reinvestment of certain foreign earnings (notably Ireland); sensitivity to tax law changes.

- Results of operations – FY2016 overview:
  - Digital Media: Leadership in Creative Cloud; ongoing shift from perpetual to subscription; Adobe Stock and Behance integrated; ARR used as key metric.
    - Creative ARR $3.54B; Document Cloud ARR $475M; total Digital Media ARR $4.01B (revalued $3.99B at FY2017 FX).
    - Creative revenue $3.18B (+38% YoY); Document Cloud $764.9M (slightly down as model transitions); total Digital Media $3.94B (+27%).
  - Digital Marketing: Adobe Marketing Cloud (Analytics, Target, Social, Media Optimizer, Experience Manager, Campaign, Audience Manager, Primetime) with record revenue $1.63B (+20%); TubeMogul expected to augment growth.

- FY2016 financial highlights:
  - Total revenue $5.85B (+22%); 53-week year vs. 52-week prior years.
  - Revenue mix: Subscription $4.585B (78% of total, +42%); Product $800.5M (14%, -29%); Services & support $469.1M (8%, +5%).
  - Deferred revenue $2.01B (+36%).
  - Cost of revenue $819.9M (+10%); operating expenses $3.54B (+12%).
  - Net income $1.17B (+86%); operating cash flow $2.20B (+50%).

- Segment performance:
  - Digital Media revenue $3.94B (67% of total, +27%).
  - Digital Marketing revenue $1.74B (30% of total, +15%).
  - Print & Publishing revenue $176.8M (3% of total, -8%).
  - 2016 vs. 2015 drivers: Creative Cloud subscriptions and ETLAs up; Acrobat perpetual down offset by Document Cloud subscriptions and Adobe Sign; Marketing Cloud growth led by AEM, Analytics, Campaign.
  - 2015 vs. 2014: Digital Media growth from Creative Cloud; stable Document Cloud; Marketing Cloud up (AEM, Campaign, Analytics, Target).

- Geography and FX:
  - Revenue by region FY2016: Americas $3.40B (58%), EMEA $1.62B (28%), APAC $0.84B (14%); growth across all regions in 2016.
  - FX headwinds: total negative impact ~$74M in 2016 and ~$135M in 2015; partial offsets from hedging.
  - Significant FX exposures hedged; notable revenue exposure to Euro, Yen, and British Pound.

- Backlog:
  - Unbilled deferred revenue backlog ~$3.4B at 12/2/16; ~40–50% not expected to be billed in FY2017; subject to timing/renewal/FX variability.

- Cost of revenue details:
  - Subscription: higher data center costs (volume growth), comp, depreciation; lower amortization of certain intangibles; higher royalties (SaaS, stock photography).
  - Product: declines in amortization/localization; higher royalties tied to stock photography.
  - Services & support: higher comp (headcount, incentives); changes in use of outside consultants.

- Operating expenses:
  - R&D $976.0M (+13%); Sales & Marketing $1,910.2M (+13%); G&A $577.7M (+9%); Amortization of purchased intangibles $78.5M (+14%); minimal restructuring.
  - Increases mainly from headcount, incentives, and marketing spend; prior year G&A benefited from reversal of a legal contingency.

- Non-operating items:
  - Interest and other income decreased vs. 2015 (prior property sale gain; higher hedging costs), partially offset by higher interest income.
  - Interest expense up on higher floating rates and average debt.
  - Small net investment losses.

- Taxes:
  - Tax provision $266.4M; effective tax rate 19% (down from 28%) due to audit completions and reinstated/permanent U.S. R&D credit; offset by stronger U.S. profits.
  - Unrecognized tax benefits $178.4M (plus ~$22.4M interest/penalties); possible $0–$10M decrease over next 12 months; 2016 audit settlements yielded ~$60.3M tax benefit.

- Liquidity and capital resources:
  - Cash & equivalents $1.01B; short-term investments $3.75B; cash/investments total $4.76B (~83% held by foreign subs); working capital $3.03B; stockholders’ equity $7.42B.
  - Cash flows FY2016: Operating $2.20B; Investing $(0.96)B (mainly investment purchases, CapEx); Financing $(1.09)B (stock repurchases).
  - Debt: $1.9B senior notes outstanding (4.75% due 2020 with interest rate swaps; 3.25% due 2025); $1B revolver available through July 2020; covenant compliant; no plans for dividends.

nodes.title: BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
nodes.heading: NOTE 1. BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
nodes.start_phrase: Founded in 1982, Adobe Systems Incorporated is one of the largest and most diversified software companies in the world.
nodes.summary:
- Company overview and operations: Adobe Systems Incorporated (founded 1982) is a diversified global software company serving creatives, marketers, developers, enterprises, and consumers via desktop, mobile, and cloud. Products are sold direct (enterprise sales, app stores, adobe.com) and through distributors, VARs, SIs, ISVs, retailers, OEMs; also via technology licensing. Significant SaaS, managed services, term subscriptions, and pay-per-use models. Operations span Americas, EMEA, and APAC.
- Basis of presentation and estimates: Consolidated Financial Statements prepared under U.S. GAAP and SEC rules; elimination of intercompany items. Significant use of estimates (sales allowances, bad debts, stock-based compensation, fair value in acquisitions, inventory, restructuring, impairments, litigation, taxes, investments).
- Fiscal year and reclassifications: 52/53-week year ending Friday closest to November 30; FY2016 included an extra week. Certain prior-year immaterial reclassifications made.
- Revenue recognition policies:
  - General criteria: persuasive evidence, delivery/performance, fixed/determinable fee, and collectibility.
  - Multiple-element arrangements: for software/software-related elements use VSOE to allocate; absent VSOE, defer revenue (except when only maintenance undelivered—recognize ratably). For non-software elements, use hierarchy VSOE/TPE/BESP and relative selling price method. For mixed software and non-software, allocate by hierarchy; recognize per applicable guidance. BESP used when standalone pricing evidence lacking; estimates consider product groups, geography, market, competition, costs, margins, pricing practices.
  - Subscriptions and services: hosted services with committed transactions recognized ratably over term; overage recognized as incurred. Consulting on time-and-materials with input/output measures; maintenance/support recognized ratably. Software subscriptions (including upgrades, hosted services, storage) recognized ratably over subscription period.
  - Product revenue: recognized on shipment subject to standard criteria; reserves for returns, rebates, and price protection; OEM royalties recognized upon OEM shipment with some estimates.
  - Rights of return/rebates/price protection: specific programs for distributors/resellers/end users; quarterly reserves based on historical trends and channel data; subscriptions largely non-cancellable with limited exceptions.
  - Revenue reserve rollforward: ending balances—$23.1M (2016), $19.4M (2015), $17.4M (2014).
  - Deferred revenue: billings/payments received before revenue recognition.
- Credit risk and receivables:
  - Allowance for doubtful accounts methodology (specific and general reserves). Rollforward ending balances—$6.2M (2016), $7.3M (2015), $7.9M (2014).
  - Credit reviews for OEMs/distributors; may recognize revenue on cash basis if collectibility not probable.
  - Concentrations: investment-grade portfolio with limits; hedging counterparties under collateral and netting arrangements; exposure to a small number of OEMs for PostScript and other licensing.
- Property and equipment: cost basis, straight-line depreciation; useful lives—computers/equipment/server capital leases 1–5 years; furniture 1–6; building improvements 5–20; buildings up to 40; leasehold improvements lesser of lease term or 1–15 years.
- Goodwill and intangibles:
  - Goodwill impairment: annual qualitative test in Q2 FY2016—no impairment; fair value assessed using market and income approaches if needed.
  - Intangible assets: amortized over 1–14 years based on consumption pattern or straight-line; no impairments in 2016–2014. Weighted average lives—purchased technology 6; customer relationships 8; trademarks 8; acquired tech rights 9; localization 1; other 4.
- Software costs:
  - Software to be sold: capitalize post-technological feasibility; amounts to date not material.
  - Internal-use software: capitalize application development stage costs (external and directly associated payroll); cease capitalization when substantially complete.
- Income taxes: asset-liability method; valuation allowances as needed. Customer taxes netted against remittances (not revenue).
- Treasury stock: cost method; gains/losses on re-issuance to APIC or retained earnings per hierarchy.
- Advertising expense: expensed as incurred—$135.8M (2016), $113.6M (2015), $87.9M (2014).
- Foreign currency:
  - Translation: local functional currencies translated to USD; CTA in AOCI.
  - Hedging: options and forwards for Euro, GBP, JPY revenues; balance sheet hedges through interest and other income; cash flow hedges’ gains/losses in OCI and reclassified to revenue upon occurrence. Aggregate net asset fair value of FX contracts $38.1M (2016) and $19.1M (2015).
- Recent accounting pronouncements:
  - ASC 606 (Revenue): effective for Adobe Q1 FY2019; no early adoption planned; most significant impact expected for term-based software licenses bundled with maintenance/support—portion of license revenue recognized upfront; continuing evaluation for services/cloud.
  - ASC 842 (Leases): effective Q1 FY2020; lessee right-of-use assets and liabilities to be recognized; evaluating impact.
  - ASU 2016-09 (Share-based payments): early adoption in Q1 FY2017; tax effects in income statement expected to add volatility to effective tax rate and EPS; will continue to estimate forfeitures.
  - No other significant new standards effective in 2016 or not yet effective.
- Acquisition:
